title: Auto Loans: Fee Share of a Scheduled Installment Payment
content:
Each scheduled payment on an Auto Loans account that PCB draws from checking toward the earliest past-due installment settles fees before anything else. This note defines the fees due used for that payment and the share of the payment they take.

## Fees due, as the loan's activity shows them

Fees due are rebuilt from the loan's own activity rather than taken from a stored balance: the total of every fee booked on the loan, of whatever kind, reduced by the total of every fee settlement and reduced again by the total of every fee waiver. The result is expressed to the cent.

## The fee share

The fee share of the payment is the smaller of two amounts: the payment amount and the fees due just defined. A payment larger than the fees due therefore clears them completely; a payment smaller than the fees due is taken wholly by fees.

## Examples (invented activity)

| Fees booked | Fee settlements | Fee waivers | Fees due | Payment amount | Fee share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 44.69 | 19.69 | 0.00 | 25.00 | 280.40 | 25.00 |
| 44.69 | 19.69 | 25.00 | 0.00 | 280.40 | 0.00 |
| 70.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 70.00 | 50.00 | 50.00 |

In the first row, one fee of 19.69 had been settled out of an earlier payment and another of 25.00 is still open, so 25.00 comes out of the new payment for fees.
